questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Molal depression constant $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}$ is given by $\frac{M_1 R T_f}{\Delta S_{f u s}}$, where symbols have their usual meaning.
Statement (II) : $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}$ for benzene is less than the $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}$ for water.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Statement-I
Molar depression constant $\mathrm{k}_f=\frac{\mathrm{M}_1 \mathrm{RT}_{\mathrm{f}}^2}{\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\text {fus }}}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{k}_f=\frac{\mathrm{M}_1 \mathrm{RT}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\left[\frac{\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\text {fus }}}{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{f}}}\right]} \\
& \mathrm{k}_f=\frac{\mathrm{M}_1 \mathrm{RT}_f}{\Delta \mathrm{~S}_{\text {fus }}}
\end{aligned}$
Hence statement-I is correct
$\text { but } \mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}} \text { for benzene }=5.12 \frac{{ }^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}}{\mathrm{molal}}$
$\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}$ for water $=1.86 \frac{{ }^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}}{\text { molal }}$ Hence statement- II is incorrect

questions.q:
Evaluate the following statements for their correctness.

A. The elevation in boiling point temperature of water will be same for $0 . 1M$~$NaCl$~and $0 . 1M$ urea.
B. Azeotropic mixture boil without change in their composition.
C. Osmosis always takes place from hypertonic to hypotonic solution.
D. The density of $32 %{H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ solution having molarity $4 . 09M$ is approximately $1 . 26g{mL}^{– 1}$.
E. A negatively charged sol is obtained when $KI$ solution is added to silver nitrate solution.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
(A) Elevation in boiling point ($∆ {T}_{b}$)~temperature of the water is not same, as ‘$i$’ value is different for two solutions.
(B) Azeotropic mixture: Liquid mixtures that distill over without changes in composition are called constant boiling mixtures or Azeotropes or Azeotropic mixtures.
(C) Osmosis always takes place from hypotonic (low concentration of solute) solution to hypertonic (high concentration of solute) solution.
(D)~Let the mass of~${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$~($32 %$) is 100.

$∴$~Weight of~${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$~=~$32$

Moles of~${H}_{2}{SO}_{4} = \dfrac{32}{98}$

Now,~$4 . 09 = \dfrac{32}{98 \times V}$

$⇒ V = 79mL$

Density =~$\dfrac{100}{79} = 1 . 265$
(E) A negative charged sol~is obtained when $KI$ solution is added to silver nitrate solution whereas positive charged sol~is obtained when~${AgNO}_{3}$~solution is added to~$KI$& solution.

So, the correct answer is B and D only.

questions.q: Liquid A and B form an ideal solution. The vapour pressure of pure liquids A and B are 350 and 750 mm Hg respectively at the same temperature. If $\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $x_B$ are the mole fraction of $A$ and $B$ in solution while $y_A$ and $y_B$ are the mole fraction of A and B in vapour phase then :
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}^{\mathrm{o}} \lt \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}^{\mathrm{o}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}^o}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}^o} \lt 1 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}^o}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}^o} \frac{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{B}}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{B}}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{B}}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Solute A associates in water. When $0 . 7g$ of solute $A$ is dissolved in $42 . 0g$ of water, it depresses the freezing point by $0 . 2 ° C$. The percentage association of solute $A$ in water, is

[Given: Molar mass of $A = 93g{mol}^{- 1}$. Molal depression constant of water is $1 . 86Kkg{mol}^{- 1}$]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Depression in freezing point,${ΔT}_{f} = {iK}_{f} \times m$

$2 . 0 = ix1 . 86 \times \dfrac{7 \times 1000}{93 \times 42}$

$2 . 0 = i \left[3 . 33\right]$

$i = 0 . 6$

$i = 1 + \left[\dfrac{1}{n} -1\right]\beta

$0 . 6 = 1 + $\left[\dfrac{1}{2} -1\right]\beta$

$\beta =0 . 8$

$% \beta =80

Hence, the percentage association of solute A in water is 80.

$

questions.q: At $35{ }^{o}C,$ the vapour pressure of $C{S}_{2},$ is $512$ mm Hg and that of acetone is $144mmHg .$ A solution of $C{S}_{2}$ in acetone has a total vapour pressure of $600mmHg$ . The false statement amongst the following is:
options: Raoult's law is not obeyed by this system
a mixture of $100mL{CS}_{2}$ and $100mL$ acetone has a volume $< 200mL$
${CS}_{2}$ and acetone are less attracted to each other than to themselves
heat must be absorbed in order to produce the solution at ${35}^{o}C$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${P}_{\text{observed}} = 600$
~
${P}_{\text{Cal}} = {P}_A^{0} {x}_{A} {\text{+P}}_B^{0} {x}_{B}$

$= 512\text{x} + 344 - 344\text{x}$

$= 168\text{x} + 344$

$= 512$ (If $\text{x} = 1$ for maximum value)

Thus, ~ ${P}_{\text{cal}} < {P}_{\text{observed}}$

Thus' the process is deviated from Raoult's law, showing positive deviation from Raoult's law.

$\Delta H > 0,$ i.e., is absorbed

questions.q: The osmotic pressure of a dilute solution of an ionic compound $XY$ in water is four times that of a solution $0.01MBaC{l}_{2}$ in water. Assuming complete dissociation of the given ionic compounds in water, the concentration of $XY$ ( $inmolL^{- 1}$ ) in solution is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Osmotic pressure $\pi = i \times CRT$

$i =$Van't~hoff factor

According to question,

for XY~$i = 2, BaC{l}_{2}$~$i = 3$

${π}_{XY} = 4 \times {\pi BaCl}_{2}$

$2 \times C \times RT = 4 \times 3 \times 0.01 \times RT$

$C = 6 \times 0.01 = 0.06M$

questions.q: The vapour pressures of pure liquids $A$ and $B$are~$400$ and $600mmHg$~respectively at $298K .$On mixing the two liquids, the sum of their volumes is equal to the volume of the final mixture. The mole fraction of liquid $B$ is $0.5$ in the mixture. The vapour pressure of the final solution, the mole fractions of components $A$ and $B$ in the vapour phase, respectively are&
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Raoult’s law& for ideal solution,

${P}_{Total} = {P}_{A} + {P}_{B}$

${P}_{Total} = {x}_{A} \times {P}_A^{∘} + {x}_{B} \times {P}_B^{∘}$

${P}_{Total} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 400 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 600 = 500mmofHg$

Dalton’s law,

${y}_{A} \times {P}_{Total} = {P}_{A}$

${y}_{A} = \dfrac{{x}_{A} \times {P}_A^{0}}{{P}_{Total}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{400}{500} = 0.4$

${y}_{B} = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$

questions.q: The quantity which changes with temperature is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Molarity$= \dfrac{No. of Moles of solute}{Volume of solution in L}$

Since volume depends on temperature, molarity will change upon change in temperature.

As the temperature rises, the volume of the solution increases. When the temperature increases the molarity of the solution will decrease as temperature depends on volume.

Hence option A is the answer.

questions.q:
Liquid $M$ and liquid $N$ form an ideal solution. The vapour pressures of pure liquids $M$ and $N$ are $450$ and $700mmHg,$ respectively, at the same temperature. Then correct statements is:
( ${x}_{M} = Molefractionof{'M}^{'}insolution;$
${x}_{N} = Molefractionof{'N}^{'}insolution;$
${y}_{M} = Molefractionof{'M}^{'}invapourphase;$
${y}_{N} = Molefractionof{'N}^{'}invapourphase;$ )
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${P}_M^{o}$~ is given as$= 450mmofHg .$

${P}_N^{o}$~ is given as$= 700mmofHg .$

We know that ${P}_{M} = {x}_{M} \times {P}_M^{O} \to$ Raoult’s law.

${P}_{N} = {x}_{N} \times {P}_N^{O} \to$ Raoult’s law.

From Dalton’s law ${P}_{M} = {y}_{M} \times {P}_{T}$

${P}_{N} = {y}_{M} \times {P}_{T}$

So,

${x}_{M} \times {P}_M^{o} = {y}_{M} \times {P}_{T} \ldots ( i )$

${x}_{M} \times {P}_N^{o} = {y}_{N} \times {P}_{T} \ldots ( ii )$

$\dfrac{( i )}{( ii )}\dfrac{xM}{xN} \times {P}_M^{o}{P}_N^{o}=\dfrac{{y}_{M}}{{y}_{N}}$

$\dfrac{{x}_{M}}{{x}_{N}} = \dfrac{{y}_{M}}{{y}_{N}} \times \dfrac{750}{450}$

$\dfrac{{x}_{M}}{{x}_{N}} > \dfrac{{y}_{M}}{{y}_{N}}$

questions.q: The mole fraction of a solvent in aqueous solution of a solute is $0.8 .$ The molality (in mol ${kg}^{- 1}$ ) of the aqueous solution is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Since mole fraction of solvent is $0.8,$ it implies that $10moles$ of aqueous solution will have $8$ moles of water and $2$ moles of solute.

$∴ 2moles$ of solute is present in $\to 8moles$ of water

Or, $2moles$ of solute is present in $\to \left(8 \times 18\right)gm$ of water

$144gm$ of water has $2$ moles of solute
$1gm$ of water will have $\dfrac{2}{144}moles$ of solute
$1$ kg of water will have $\dfrac{2}{144} \times 1000 = 13.88moles$

$∴$ Molality = $13.88m$

questions.q: Consider a binary solution of two volatile liquid components 1 and $2 . x_1$ and $y_1$ are the mole fractions of component 1 in liquid and vapour phase, respectively. The slope and intercept of the linear plot of $\frac{1}{x_1}$ vs $\frac{1}{y_1}$ are given respectively as:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given mole fraction of liquid 1 in liquid and vapour phase is $x_1$ and $y_1$ respectively.
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}_1=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}} y_1=\mathrm{P}_1^0 x_1 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}}{x_1}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_1^0}{y_1} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{P}_2^0+x_1\left(\mathrm{P}_1^0+\mathrm{P}_2^0\right)}{x_1}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_1^0}{y_1} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{P}_2^0}{x_1}+\left(\mathrm{P}_1^0+\mathrm{P}_2^0\right)=\frac{\mathrm{P}_1^0}{y_1} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{P}_2^0}{x_1}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_1^0}{y_1}-\left(\mathrm{P}_1^0+\mathrm{P}_2^0\right) \\ & \frac{1}{x_1}=\frac{1}{y_2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_1^0}{\mathrm{P}_2^0}\right)-\frac{\left(\mathrm{P}_1^0+\mathrm{P}_2^0\right)}{\mathrm{P}_2^0}\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{x_1}=\frac{1}{y_2}\left(\frac{P_1^0}{P_2^0}\right)+\frac{\left(P_2^0-P_1^0\right)}{P_2^0} \\ & y=m x+c \\ & \text { Slope }=\frac{P_1^0}{P_2^0} ; \text { Intercept }=\frac{P_2^0-P_1^0}{P_2^0}\end{aligned}$$
